title: BigQuery Slot Usage Monitoring

controlTest.positiveScenario: Replay sample `google:gcp:monitoring` events with `metric.type="bigquery.googleapis.com/slot/usage"` into `index=gcp`. Confirm UC-4.3.25 returns >=1 row and the alert fires.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Replay benign `google:gcp:monitoring` traffic without `metric.type="bigquery.googleapis.com/slot/usage"`. Confirm UC-4.3.25 returns zero rows and the alert does not fire.

dataSources: `index=gcp` sourcetype=`google:gcp:monitoring` collected via `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`, BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA export; validate ingest with `| stats count by sourcetype`.
spl:
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="bigquery.googleapis.com/slot/usage"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.25_bigquery_slot_usage_moni_25"
| sort -_time
description: UC-4.3.25 — BigQuery Slot Usage Monitoring: queries Google Cloud `google:gcp:monitoring` for search criteria `metric.type="bigquery.googleapis.com/slot/usage"` and returns actor, resource, and region context for capacity review and change validation.
value: On Google Cloud, detecting 'BigQuery Slot Usage Monitoring' early shortens cloud incident response and produces defensible audit evidence for identity and change-management controls. UC-4.3.25 drives high-priority capacity alerting before customer-impacting drift.
implementation: Ingest Cloud Monitoring metrics for slot usage and optional `JOBS_BY_PROJECT` exports. Alert when usage exceeds reservation plus burst buffer or sustained elevation vs 7-day baseline. Dashboard by reservation assignment and job type.
visualization: Area chart (slot usage vs cap), Table (project, peak slots), Single value (utilization %).
cimSpl:
| tstats `summariesonly` avg(Performance.cpu_load_percent) as agg_value
  from datamodel=Performance where nodename=Performance.CPU
  by Performance.host span=5m
| sort - agg_value
dataModelAcceleration: Enable data model acceleration for Performance (CPU node).
knownFalsePositives: Short spikes at deploy time, autoscale thrash, or a noisy neighbor on shared hosts can look bad for a few minutes. We require the condition to last across several intervals or clear on its own before we wake someone.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Splunk Enterprise or Splunk Cloud with search access to `index=gcp`.
• Install and configure `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`, BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA export with the modular input for `google:gcp:monitoring`.
• Prerequisite crawl UC(s): UC-4.3.41.
• Confirm field extractions in `props.conf` for `resource.type` and related actor fields.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Ingest Cloud Monitoring metrics for slot usage and optional `JOBS_BY_PROJECT` exports. Alert when usage exceeds reservation plus burst buffer or sustained elevation vs 7-day baseline. Dashboard by reservation assignment and job type.
Validate ingest before alerting:
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" | stats count by sourcetype
```

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=gcp sourcetype="google:gcp:monitoring" metric.type="bigquery.googleapis.com/slot/usage"
| table _time resource.type metric.type value
| eval uc_marker="UC-4.3.25_bigquery_slot_usage_moni_25"
| sort -_time
```

Understanding this SPL
Scopes `google:gcp:monitoring` in `index=gcp` to detect bigquery slot usage monitoring. Tune thresholds to your change cadence; exclude break-glass principals and sandbox accounts via a lookup.

Step 3 — Validate
Compare to the provider cloud console audit view for the same 24-hour window. Confirm row counts and `resource.type` values match the vendor console. Run `| fieldsummary` on a 1-hour sample to verify extractions.

Step 4 — Operationalize and troubleshoot
Save as `4_3_25_alert` with severity aligned to `high` criticality. Dashboard: Area chart (slot usage vs cap), Table (project, peak slots), Single value (utilization %)..
Failure modes: (1) no events — verify modular input/API credentials and index routing; (2) empty actor fields — upgrade `Splunk_TA_google-cloudplatform`, BigQuery INFORMATION_SCHEMA export and review alias mappings; (3) API throttling — reduce poll frequency or enable queue buffering; (4) alert fatigue — tune thresholds and document exclusions in knownFalsePositives.
grandmaExplanation: We watch cloud logs for signs of bigquery slot usage monitoring so your team catches problems in your online services before customers or auditors do.
